RE-1.t: Explain how SRY on the Y chromosome drives the bipotential gonad to form testes with Sertoli cells, and predict the gonadal phenotype of a 46,XY embryo with an SRY deletion or a 46,XX embryo with an SRY translocation.

Relate Sertoli cell anti-Mullerian hormone, Leydig cell testosterone, and dihydrotestosterone (DHT) to Mullerian duct regression, Wolffian duct development, and masculinization of the external genitalia and prostate.

Trace the paramesonephric (Mullerian) ducts to the uterine tubes, uterus, cervix, and upper vagina, and explain how failed fusion or failed septum resorption produces uterus didelphys, bicornuate uterus, and septate uterus.
RE-1.usmle: Female and Transgender Reproductive System & Breast: Congenital: uterus didelphys, bicornuate uterus

RE-1.t: Match the male and female derivatives of the genital tubercle (glans penis, clitoris), urogenital folds (ventral penile shaft and penile urethra, labia minora), and labioscrotal swellings (scrotum, labia majora).
Describe testicular descent guided by the gubernaculum through the inguinal canal, and explain how a patent processus vaginalis leads to an indirect inguinal hernia or a communicating hydrocele.
RE-1.usmle: Male and Transgender Reproductive System: Traumatic and mechanical: hydrocele (including neonatal)

RE-1.t: Describe placental formation from the fetal chorion frondosum (cytotrophoblast and syncytiotrophoblast) and maternal decidua basalis, and identify the umbilical cord vessels (two umbilical arteries, one umbilical vein) in Wharton jelly.

Describe breast development from the ectodermal mammary ridge (milk line), and explain how incomplete regression of the ridge produces supernumerary nipples or breast tissue between the axilla and the groin.

RE-2.t: Distinguish Sertoli cells (tight junctions forming the blood-testis barrier, androgen-binding protein, inhibin B) from interstitial Leydig cells (testosterone) on testis histology.
Trace sperm from the seminiferous tubules through the rete testis, efferent ductules, epididymis, ductus deferens, ejaculatory duct, and prostatic, membranous, and spongy urethra.

Identify the epithelium of each female tract segment (ciliated simple columnar uterine tube, simple columnar endometrium and endocervix, stratified squamous ectocervix and vagina) and locate the transformation zone where cervical dysplasia arises.
RE-2.usmle: Female and Transgender Reproductive System & Breast: Neoplasms, malignant and precancerous: cervical dysplasia

RE-2.t: Distinguish primordial, primary, secondary (antral), and mature (Graafian) follicles and the corpus luteum by their oocyte, granulosa cell, and theca cell features.
Describe the breast terminal duct lobular unit, with luminal epithelial cells over a myoepithelial cell layer, and relate it to the origin of most breast carcinomas and fibroadenomas.
RE-2.usmle: Female and Transgender Reproductive System & Breast: Breast: Malignant neoplasms: breast cancer

RE-2.t: Describe the peripheral, transition, and central zones of the prostate, and relate benign prostatic hyperplasia to the transition zone and most prostate carcinomas to the peripheral zone.
RE-2.usmle: Male and Transgender Reproductive System: Neoplasms: prostate cancer

RE-3.t: Compare spermatogenesis and oogenesis, including oocyte arrest in prophase I until ovulation and in metaphase II until fertilization, and the number of functional gametes produced from each meiosis.

Describe spermiogenesis (acrosome from the Golgi apparatus, flagellum from a centriole, shedding of cytoplasm), and explain capacitation in the female tract and the acrosome reaction required for fertilization.
Explain fertilization in the ampulla of the uterine tube, including the cortical reaction that blocks polyspermy and completion of the second meiotic division.
Trace the conceptus from zygote to blastocyst, and explain implantation into the endometrium about day 6 with syncytiotrophoblast invasion and hCG secretion that maintains the corpus luteum.
Predict the consequences of abnormal implantation, including tubal ectopic pregnancy (most often ampullary, with prior salpingitis as a risk factor) and placenta previa over the internal cervical os.
RE-3.usmle: Pregnancy, Childbirth, & the Puerperium: Obstetric complications: ectopic pregnancy

RE-3.t: Describe formation of the bilaminar disc in week 2 and the trilaminar disc by gastrulation in week 3, and explain why weeks 3 to 8 are the period of greatest teratogen sensitivity.
RE-3.usmle: Pregnancy, Childbirth, & the Puerperium: Adverse effects of drugs: teratology

RE-4.t: Describe the broad ligament and its parts (mesometrium, mesosalpinx, mesovarium), and identify the rectouterine pouch as the lowest peritoneal recess where blood or pus collects in a standing woman.

Identify the suspensory (infundibulopelvic) ligament carrying the ovarian vessels, the ovarian ligament, the round ligament through the inguinal canal, the cardinal ligament carrying the uterine vessels, and the uterosacral ligaments.
Describe uterine and vaginal support by the levator ani, perineal body, and cardinal and uterosacral ligaments, and relate weakening of these supports to uterine prolapse and pelvic relaxation.
RE-4.usmle: Female and Transgender Reproductive System & Breast: Traumatic and mechanical: pelvic relaxation

RE-4.t: List the layers of the scrotum and spermatic cord (skin, dartos, external spermatic fascia, cremaster, internal spermatic fascia, tunica vaginalis) and the cord contents, including the ductus deferens, testicular artery, and pampiniform plexus.
Describe the breast over the pectoralis major from about rib 2 to rib 6 with an axillary tail, and explain skin dimpling when carcinoma involves the suspensory (Cooper) ligaments.
RE-4.usmle: Female and Transgender Reproductive System & Breast: Breast: Malignant neoplasms: breast cancer

RE-4.t: Locate the paired corpora cavernosa, the corpus spongiosum surrounding the urethra, and the tunica albuginea, and relate rupture of the tunica albuginea to penile fracture.
RE-4.usmle: Male and Transgender Reproductive System: Traumatic and mechanical: penile fracture

RE-4.t: Describe the perineum, bounded by the pubic symphysis, ischiopubic rami, ischial tuberosities, sacrotuberous ligaments, and coccyx and divided into urogenital and anal triangles, and locate the prostate below the bladder and in front of the rectum for digital rectal exam.

RE-5.t: Trace the gonadal arteries from the abdominal aorta and the gonadal veins (left to the left renal vein, right to the inferior vena cava), and explain why varicocele is more common on the left.
RE-5.usmle: Male and Transgender Reproductive System: Traumatic and mechanical: varicocele

RE-5.t: Trace the uterine artery from the anterior division of the internal iliac artery, and explain why the ureter, passing beneath the uterine artery near the cervix, is at risk during ligation of these vessels.

Compare lymph drainage of the testis and ovary (para-aortic nodes), uterus, cervix, and proximal vagina (internal and external iliac nodes), and scrotum, vulva, and distal vagina (superficial inguinal nodes), and predict nodal spread of tumors.
RE-5.usmle: Male and Transgender Reproductive System: Neoplasms: testicular cancer

RE-5.t: Describe the nerves of the male sexual response: erection by parasympathetic pelvic splanchnic nerves (S2 to S4), emission by sympathetic hypogastric nerves, and ejaculation by the somatic pudendal nerve.
RE-5.usmle: Male and Transgender Reproductive System: Metabolic/regulatory and sexual dysfunction: erectile dysfunction

RE-5.t: Trace the pudendal nerve (S2 to S4) out the greater sciatic foramen, around the ischial spine, and through the lesser sciatic foramen to the perineum, and identify the ischial spine as its landmark.

Describe breast blood supply from the internal thoracic, lateral thoracic, and thoracoacromial arteries, and lymph drainage mostly to axillary nodes with medial quadrants also draining to parasternal nodes.
RE-5.usmle: Female and Transgender Reproductive System & Breast: Breast: Malignant neoplasms: breast cancer

RE-6.t: Relate the follicular and luteal phases of the ovarian cycle to the proliferative, secretory, and menstrual phases of the endometrium, and explain why the luteal phase stays near 14 days while cycle length varies.
Explain erection as nitric oxide release raising cGMP in cavernosal smooth muscle, causing relaxation, arterial inflow, and compression of venous outflow against the tunica albuginea.
RE-6.usmle: Male and Transgender Reproductive System: Metabolic/regulatory and sexual dysfunction: erectile dysfunction

RE-6.t: Explain how hCG maintains the corpus luteum until the placenta takes over progesterone production near the end of the first trimester, and why placental estriol synthesis depends on fetal adrenal DHEA-S.

Predict the maternal adaptations of pregnancy: plasma volume rising more than red cell mass (dilutional anemia), higher cardiac output, lower systemic vascular resistance, higher GFR, respiratory alkalosis, and hypercoagulability.
RE-6.usmle: Pregnancy, Childbirth, & the Puerperium: Obstetric complications: anemia of pregnancy

RE-6.t: Explain how human placental lactogen and other placental hormones increase maternal insulin resistance, and relate this to the development of gestational diabetes.
RE-6.usmle: Pregnancy, Childbirth, & the Puerperium: Obstetric complications: gestational diabetes

RE-6.t: Explain lactation: alveolar development under estrogen, progesterone, and prolactin, milk secretion after placental progesterone withdrawal, suckling-driven prolactin (synthesis) and oxytocin (myoepithelial ejection), and suckling suppression of GnRH.
RE-6.usmle: Pregnancy, Childbirth, & the Puerperium: Puerperium: lactation problems

RE-6.t: Explain the positive feedback of parturition, in which cervical stretch increases oxytocin release (Ferguson reflex) and oxytocin and prostaglandins increase myometrial contraction.
RE-6.usmle: Pregnancy, Childbirth, & the Puerperium: Labor and delivery: labor and delivery, uncomplicated

RE-7.t: Explain how pulsatile GnRH stimulates LH and FSH release, and predict why continuous GnRH exposure suppresses gonadotropin secretion.

Explain the male axis: LH stimulates Leydig cell testosterone, FSH stimulates Sertoli cell androgen-binding protein and inhibin B, with negative feedback by testosterone on LH and by inhibin B on FSH.

Explain the two-cell model of ovarian steroidogenesis (LH drives theca cell androgen, FSH drives granulosa cell aromatase), and how sustained high estradiol switches to positive feedback to trigger the LH surge.
Describe sex steroid transport bound to SHBG and albumin, and predict how SHBG changes (raised by estrogen, lowered by androgens, insulin resistance, and obesity) alter free testosterone.

Distinguish DHT actions (external genitalia, prostate, male-pattern hair loss) from testosterone actions (Wolffian ducts, spermatogenesis, muscle mass, libido), and describe estrogen and progesterone effects on target tissues.
Describe puberty as reactivation of pulsatile GnRH secretion, beginning with sleep-associated LH pulses, and list the usual female sequence of thelarche, pubarche, growth spurt, and menarche.
Explain prolactin regulation by tonic hypothalamic dopamine inhibition, and predict how hyperprolactinemia suppresses GnRH to cause amenorrhea, galactorrhea, and hypogonadism.
RE-7.usmle: Female and Transgender Reproductive System & Breast: Menstrual and endocrine: secondary amenorrhea

RE-8.t: Trace sex steroid synthesis from cholesterol to pregnenolone (cholesterol side-chain cleavage), then to progesterone, androstenedione, testosterone, and estradiol, naming 3-beta-hydroxysteroid dehydrogenase, 17-alpha-hydroxylase, 17,20-lyase, 17-beta-hydroxysteroid dehydrogenase, and aromatase.
Explain the conversion of testosterone to DHT by 5-alpha-reductase in genital skin and prostate, and predict ambiguous genitalia at birth with virilization at puberty in 5-alpha-reductase deficiency.
Explain peripheral aromatization of androstenedione to estrone in adipose tissue, and relate obesity to unopposed estrogen, endometrial hyperplasia, and gynecomastia.
RE-8.usmle: Female and Transgender Reproductive System & Breast: Neoplasms, malignant and precancerous: endometrial hyperplasia

RE-8.t: Describe hCG, LH, FSH, and TSH as glycoproteins sharing a common alpha subunit with hormone-specific beta subunits, and explain why very high hCG in molar pregnancy can cause hyperthyroidism.
RE-8.usmle: Female and Transgender Reproductive System & Breast: Neoplasms, malignant and precancerous: gestational trophoblastic disease

RE-8.t: Describe hepatic inactivation of sex steroids by conjugation to glucuronides and sulfates for excretion, and explain why cirrhosis causes gynecomastia, spider angiomas, palmar erythema, and testicular atrophy.

Identify the seminal vesicle (fructose) and prostatic (PSA, a serine protease that liquefies the semen coagulum; citrate; zinc) contributions to semen, and explain why PSA rises in prostatitis and BPH as well as carcinoma.
RE-8.usmle: Male and Transgender Reproductive System: Neoplasms: prostate cancer

RE-9.t: Explain the role of folate in thymidylate and purine synthesis, and relate maternal folate deficiency to neural tube defects, which arise when the neural tube fails to close by about day 28.
RE-9.usmle: Pregnancy, Childbirth, & the Puerperium: Prenatal care: folate deficiency prevention; neural tube defects

RE-9.t: Explain the higher iron requirement of pregnancy (expanded red cell mass, fetal and placental needs), and distinguish iron deficiency from physiologic dilutional anemia using ferritin and MCV.
RE-9.usmle: Pregnancy, Childbirth, & the Puerperium: Prenatal care: iron deficiency prevention

RE-9.t: Describe lactose synthesis by lactose synthase (galactosyltransferase with alpha-lactalbumin), and compare human milk content of lactose, whey proteins, and secretory IgA with its low vitamin D and vitamin K.
RE-9.usmle: Pregnancy, Childbirth, & the Puerperium: Puerperium: breast-feeding problems

RE-9.t: Explain placental glucose transfer by facilitated diffusion while maternal insulin does not cross, and predict fetal hyperinsulinemia, macrosomia, and neonatal hypoglycemia from maternal hyperglycemia.
RE-9.usmle: Pregnancy, Childbirth, & the Puerperium: Obstetric complications: gestational diabetes

RE-9.t: Relate zinc deficiency to hypogonadism and delayed sexual maturation, and excess vitamin A (including retinoids) to teratogenic craniofacial, cardiac, and central nervous system defects.
Explain how low energy availability and low leptin in athletes or people with very low body fat suppress GnRH pulsatility, causing hypothalamic amenorrhea and loss of bone density.
RE-9.usmle: Female and Transgender Reproductive System & Breast: Menstrual and endocrine: secondary amenorrhea

RE-9.t: Explain how the gonads and placenta obtain cholesterol for steroid synthesis mainly by LDL receptor-mediated uptake, and identify StAR-mediated transfer of cholesterol into mitochondria as the rate-limiting step in gonadal steroidogenesis.

RE-10.t: Explain how meiotic nondisjunction produces 47,XXY and 45,X karyotypes, and how nondisjunction after fertilization produces mosaicism with milder phenotypes.
RE-10.usmle: Male and Transgender Reproductive System: Congenital: Klinefelter syndrome

RE-10.t: Explain X inactivation by XIST with Barr body formation, and predict the number of Barr bodies in 46,XX, 47,XXY, and 45,X cells.
Explain how high-risk HPV E6 promotes p53 degradation and E7 binds and inactivates Rb to release E2F, removing cell cycle checkpoints in cervical epithelium.
RE-10.usmle: Female and Transgender Reproductive System & Breast: Neoplasms, malignant and precancerous: HPV-caused cancer

RE-10.t: Relate autosomal dominant BRCA1 and BRCA2 mutations (homologous recombination DNA repair genes) to hereditary breast and ovarian cancer, and BRCA2 to male breast and prostate cancer.
RE-10.usmle: Female and Transgender Reproductive System & Breast: Breast: Malignant neoplasms: breast cancer

RE-10.t: Relate Lynch syndrome (germline mismatch repair gene mutations, microsatellite instability) to endometrial and ovarian carcinoma as well as colorectal carcinoma.
RE-10.usmle: Multisystem Processes & Disorders: hereditary nonpolyposis colorectal cancer (gastrointestinal and female reproductive)

RE-10.t: Classify breast carcinomas by estrogen receptor, progesterone receptor, and HER2 (ERBB2 amplification) status, and relate triple-negative basal-like tumors to BRCA1 mutation.
RE-10.usmle: Female and Transgender Reproductive System & Breast: Breast: Malignant neoplasms: breast cancer

RE-11.t: Explain testicular immune privilege (Sertoli cell blood-testis barrier, local immunosuppression), predict antisperm antibodies after trauma, vasectomy, or mumps orchitis, and describe autoimmune orchitis as a cause of hypogonadism.
RE-11.usmle: Male and Transgender Reproductive System: Immunologic: autoimmune hypogonadism

RE-11.t: Explain maternal tolerance of the semiallogeneic fetus, including trophoblast expression of nonclassical HLA-G in place of HLA-A and HLA-B, which limits maternal T cell and NK cell attack.
Explain passive immunity of the newborn through FcRn-mediated placental transfer of maternal IgG (not IgM) and secretory IgA in breast milk.

Explain Rh alloimmunization, in which an Rh-negative mother forms anti-D IgG after fetomaternal hemorrhage, causing type II hypersensitivity hemolysis and possible hydrops fetalis in a later Rh-positive fetus.
RE-11.usmle: Pregnancy, Childbirth, & the Puerperium: Obstetric complications: Rh isoimmunization

RE-11.t: Describe vaginal defenses (lactobacilli producing lactic acid to keep pH at or below 4.5, secretory IgA), and predict overgrowth of Gardnerella and anaerobes when lactobacilli are lost.
RE-11.usmle: Female and Transgender Reproductive System & Breast: Infectious, immunologic, and inflammatory: bacterial vaginosis

RE-11.t: Explain how HPV vaccines made of L1 capsid virus-like particles induce neutralizing antibodies, and how cell-mediated immunity clears most HPV infections and low-grade lesions, so that immunosuppression such as HIV raises cervical cancer risk.
RE-11.usmle: Female and Transgender Reproductive System & Breast: Infectious, immunologic, and inflammatory: human papillomavirus infection

RE-11.t: Explain how the inflammatory response to repeated or untreated chlamydial and gonococcal salpingitis causes tubal scarring, increasing the risk of infertility and ectopic pregnancy.
RE-11.usmle: Female and Transgender Reproductive System & Breast: Fertility and infertility: tubal factors

RE-12.t: Describe Neisseria gonorrhoeae as an oxidase-positive gram-negative diplococcus that ferments glucose but not maltose, with pili showing antigenic variation, IgA protease, and lipooligosaccharide, cultured on Thayer-Martin agar.
RE-12.usmle: Female and Transgender Reproductive System & Breast: Infectious, immunologic, and inflammatory: gonorrhea (Neisseria gonorrhoeae)

RE-12.t: Describe Chlamydia trachomatis as an obligate intracellular bacterium with an infectious elementary body and replicating reticulate body, and match serovars A to C (trachoma), D to K (genital and neonatal), and L1 to L3 (LGV).
RE-12.usmle: Female and Transgender Reproductive System & Breast: Infectious, immunologic, and inflammatory: lymphogranuloma venereum (Chlamydia trachomatis)

RE-12.t: Describe Treponema pallidum as a thin spirochete that cannot be cultured on standard media, seen by dark-field microscopy, and transmitted sexually and transplacentally.
RE-12.usmle: Female and Transgender Reproductive System & Breast: Infectious, immunologic, and inflammatory: syphilis (Treponema pallidum)

RE-12.t: Compare HSV-2 (enveloped dsDNA herpesvirus with latency in sacral sensory ganglia) with HPV (nonenveloped dsDNA papillomavirus), distinguishing low-risk types 6 and 11 from high-risk types 16 and 18.
RE-12.usmle: Female and Transgender Reproductive System & Breast: Infectious, immunologic, and inflammatory: genital herpes; human papillomavirus infection

RE-12.t: Identify Trichomonas vaginalis (motile flagellated protozoan on wet mount), Candida albicans (yeast with pseudohyphae on KOH preparation), and Gardnerella vaginalis (clue cells) by their microscopic features.
RE-12.usmle: Female and Transgender Reproductive System & Breast: Infectious, immunologic, and inflammatory: vaginitis

RE-12.t: Describe Haemophilus ducreyi as a gram-negative coccobacillus, and explain how Staphylococcus aureus TSST-1 acts as a superantigen by binding MHC class II and the T cell receptor outside the antigen groove.
RE-12.usmle: Female and Transgender Reproductive System & Breast: Infectious, immunologic, and inflammatory: chancroid (Haemophilus ducreyi)

RE-12.t: Describe Streptococcus agalactiae (group B, beta-hemolytic, CAMP positive, bacitracin resistant) colonizing the vagina, and identify the TORCH organisms transmitted across the placenta or during delivery.
RE-12.usmle: Pregnancy, Childbirth, & the Puerperium: Prenatal care: infections, maternal, fetal, newborn

RE-13-A.t: Distinguish primary amenorrhea (no menarche by age 15, or by 13 without breast development) from secondary amenorrhea (no menses for 3 months after regular cycles), naming pregnancy as the most common cause of secondary amenorrhea.
RE-13-A.usmle: Female and Transgender Reproductive System & Breast: Menstrual and endocrine: primary amenorrhea; secondary amenorrhea

RE-13-A.t: Interpret FSH, LH, prolactin, TSH, and estradiol levels to localize amenorrhea to the hypothalamus (low FSH and LH), pituitary, ovary (high FSH), or outflow tract, such as Asherman syndrome.
RE-13-A.usmle: Female and Transgender Reproductive System & Breast: Traumatic and mechanical: Asherman syndrome

RE-13-A.t: Explain anovulation from absent LH surge or disordered follicle development (PCOS, hyperprolactinemia, thyroid disease, low energy availability), and predict unopposed estrogen effects of irregular heavy bleeding and endometrial hyperplasia.
RE-13-A.usmle: Female and Transgender Reproductive System & Breast: Menstrual and endocrine: anovulation

RE-13-A.t: Explain anovulatory bleeding (formerly dysfunctional uterine bleeding, now abnormal uterine bleeding from ovulatory dysfunction in the PALM-COEIN system) as estrogen-driven proliferation without progesterone-induced secretory change, and distinguish it from structural causes such as polyps, adenomyosis, leiomyoma, and malignancy.
RE-13-A.usmle: Female and Transgender Reproductive System & Breast: Menstrual and endocrine: abnormal uterine bleeding

RE-13-A.t: Explain menopause as follicle depletion with loss of estradiol and inhibin feedback, raising FSH and LH, and relate estrogen loss to vasomotor symptoms, atrophic vaginitis, osteoporosis, and higher cardiovascular risk.
RE-13-A.usmle: Female and Transgender Reproductive System & Breast: Menopause: perimenopause; vasomotor symptoms; postmenopausal atrophic vaginitis

RE-13-A.t: Describe primary ovarian insufficiency (ovarian failure before age 40) with causes including Turner syndrome, FMR1 premutation, autoimmune oophoritis, and chemotherapy or radiation, and its high FSH and low estradiol profile.
RE-13-A.usmle: Female and Transgender Reproductive System & Breast: Menopause: ovarian failure; premature menopause

RE-13-A.t: Distinguish hirsutism from virilization, and localize androgen excess to the ovary (PCOS, Sertoli-Leydig cell tumor) or adrenal (congenital adrenal hyperplasia, adrenal tumor) using testosterone and DHEA-S levels.
RE-13-A.usmle: Female and Transgender Reproductive System & Breast: Menstrual and endocrine: hirsutism; virilization

RE-13-A.t: Explain primary dysmenorrhea as prostaglandin-driven myometrial contraction and ischemia, and mittelschmerz as midcycle pain at ovulation from follicle rupture.
RE-13-A.usmle: Female and Transgender Reproductive System & Breast: Menstrual and endocrine: dysmenorrhea; mittelschmerz

RE-13-A.t: Classify female infertility as ovulatory (PCOS, hyperprolactinemia, ovarian insufficiency), tubal (prior PID), or uterine (Asherman syndrome, submucosal leiomyoma), and explain the mechanism of each.
RE-13-A.usmle: Female and Transgender Reproductive System & Breast: Fertility and infertility: female infertility

RE-13-B.t: Describe balanitis as inflammation of the glans penis, most often from Candida or bacteria, with risk factors of an uncircumcised foreskin, poor hygiene, and diabetes mellitus, and relate recurrent balanitis to phimosis.
RE-13-B.usmle: Male and Transgender Reproductive System: Infectious, immunologic, and inflammatory: balanitis

RE-13-B.t: Identify Chlamydia trachomatis and Neisseria gonorrhoeae as the main causes of mucopurulent cervicitis, and distinguish it from the punctate hemorrhagic strawberry cervix of trichomoniasis and the ulcerative cervicitis of HSV.
RE-13-B.usmle: Female and Transgender Reproductive System & Breast: Infectious, immunologic, and inflammatory: cervicitis; endocervicitis

RE-13-B.t: Explain endometriosis as endometrial glands and stroma outside the uterus (theories of retrograde menstruation, coelomic metaplasia, vascular or lymphatic spread), and relate ovarian chocolate cysts and adhesions to dysmenorrhea, dyspareunia, and infertility.
RE-13-B.usmle: Female and Transgender Reproductive System & Breast: Menstrual and endocrine: endometriosis

RE-13-B.t: Distinguish adenomyosis (endometrial glands and stroma within the myometrium, causing a uniformly enlarged, tender uterus with dysmenorrhea and heavy bleeding) from endometriosis and leiomyoma.
RE-13-B.usmle: Female and Transgender Reproductive System & Breast: Menstrual and endocrine: dysmenorrhea

RE-13-B.t: Distinguish acute endometritis (polymicrobial infection after delivery, miscarriage, or retained products, with fever and uterine tenderness) from chronic endometritis, identified by plasma cells in the endometrial stroma.
RE-13-B.usmle: Pregnancy, Childbirth, & the Puerperium: Puerperium: postpartum sepsis

RE-13-B.t: Distinguish mumps orchitis (postpubertal, risk of testicular atrophy and infertility) from epididymo-orchitis caused by C. trachomatis or N. gonorrhoeae in sexually active young men and by E. coli in older men.
RE-13-B.usmle: Male and Transgender Reproductive System: Infectious, immunologic, and inflammatory: epididymitis; orchitis

RE-13-B.t: Explain pelvic inflammatory disease as ascending infection by C. trachomatis, N. gonorrhoeae, and vaginal flora, and identify cervical motion tenderness, adnexal tenderness, fever, and purulent cervical discharge.
RE-13-B.usmle: Female and Transgender Reproductive System & Breast: Infectious, immunologic, and inflammatory: pelvic inflammatory disease

RE-13-B.t: Predict the complications of salpingitis, including hydrosalpinx, tubo-ovarian abscess, tubal infertility, ectopic pregnancy, and Fitz-Hugh-Curtis perihepatitis with right upper quadrant pain and violin-string adhesions.
RE-13-B.usmle: Female and Transgender Reproductive System & Breast: Infectious, immunologic, and inflammatory: salpingitis; Fitz-Hugh-Curtis syndrome

RE-13-B.t: Relate candidal vaginitis to risk factors (diabetes, antibiotic use, pregnancy, immunosuppression), and identify thick white curd-like discharge, vulvar itching, normal vaginal pH, and pseudohyphae on KOH preparation.
RE-13-B.usmle: Female and Transgender Reproductive System & Breast: Infectious, immunologic, and inflammatory: candidiasis of vulva or vagina

RE-13-B.t: Describe lichen sclerosus as thinned epidermis with dermal fibrosis forming white parchment-like vulvar plaques, mostly in postmenopausal women, and relate it to a small increase in vulvar squamous cell carcinoma risk.
RE-13-B.usmle: Female and Transgender Reproductive System & Breast: Infectious, immunologic, and inflammatory: lichen sclerosus

RE-13-C.t: Describe cryptorchidism (most often inguinal, more common in preterm infants), and relate it to impaired spermatogenesis from higher temperature, reduced inhibin B with raised FSH, and increased germ cell tumor risk.
RE-13-C.usmle: Male and Transgender Reproductive System: Congenital: undescended testicle

RE-13-C.t: Compare hypospadias (ventral urethral opening from failed fusion of the urethral folds, associated with cryptorchidism and inguinal hernia) with epispadias (dorsal opening from abnormal genital tubercle position, associated with bladder exstrophy).
RE-13-C.usmle: Male and Transgender Reproductive System: Congenital: hypospadias

RE-13-C.t: Explain fragile X syndrome as an FMR1 CGG repeat expansion with hypermethylation and silencing, showing anticipation through maternal transmission, and identify intellectual disability, postpubertal macroorchidism, long face, large jaw, and large ears.
RE-13-C.usmle: Multisystem Processes & Disorders: Genetic, metabolic, and developmental disorders: triplet repeat/RNA disorders: fragile X syndrome

RE-13-C.t: Explain imperforate hymen as failure of the hymen to perforate during development, and predict primary amenorrhea with cyclic pelvic pain, a bulging bluish membrane, and hematocolpos at menarche.
RE-13-C.usmle: Female and Transgender Reproductive System & Breast: Traumatic and mechanical: imperforate hymen

RE-13-C.t: Explain Klinefelter syndrome (47,XXY) as seminiferous tubule dysgenesis (low inhibin B, high FSH) with Leydig cell dysfunction (low testosterone, high LH), and identify small firm testes, tall stature, gynecomastia, and infertility.
RE-13-C.usmle: Male and Transgender Reproductive System: Congenital: Klinefelter syndrome

RE-13-C.t: Distinguish phimosis (foreskin that cannot be retracted over the glans, physiologic in infancy or acquired from scarring) from paraphimosis (retracted foreskin trapped behind the glans, causing edema and ischemia).
RE-13-C.usmle: Male and Transgender Reproductive System: Traumatic and mechanical: phimosis

RE-13-C.t: Distinguish 46,XX disorders of sex development (DSD), formerly female pseudohermaphroditism (ovaries with virilized genitalia from 21-hydroxylase deficiency or excess maternal androgen), from 46,XY DSD, formerly male pseudohermaphroditism (testes with undervirilized genitalia from androgen insensitivity or 5-alpha-reductase deficiency).
RE-13-C.usmle: Endocrine System: Congenital disorders: disorders of sexual differentiation

RE-13-C.t: Explain complete androgen insensitivity (X-linked androgen receptor defect) with female external genitalia, blind vaginal pouch, absent uterus and tubes, undescended testes, sparse pubic hair, and raised testosterone, estrogen, and LH.
RE-13-C.usmle: Endocrine System: Congenital disorders: disorders of sexual differentiation

RE-13-C.t: Distinguish Mullerian agenesis (46,XX, normal ovaries and pubic hair, absent uterus and upper vagina) from complete androgen insensitivity as causes of primary amenorrhea with a blind vaginal pouch.
RE-13-C.usmle: Female and Transgender Reproductive System & Breast: Congenital: mullerian agenesis

RE-13-C.t: Explain septate uterus as failed resorption of the midline septum after Mullerian duct fusion and a cause of recurrent pregnancy loss, and describe longitudinal and transverse vaginal septa from abnormal fusion or canalization.
Explain Turner syndrome (45,X or mosaic) as ovarian dysgenesis with streak ovaries, and predict primary amenorrhea, absent breast development, low estradiol, and high FSH and LH.
RE-13-C.usmle: Female and Transgender Reproductive System & Breast: Fertility and infertility: Turner syndrome

RE-13-C.t: Identify the associated findings of Turner syndrome: short stature (SHOX loss), webbed neck from fetal cystic hygroma, lymphedema of hands and feet, bicuspid aortic valve, coarctation of the aorta, and horseshoe kidney.
RE-13-C.usmle: Female and Transgender Reproductive System & Breast: Fertility and infertility: Turner syndrome

RE-13-D.t: Classify erectile dysfunction as vascular (atherosclerosis), neurogenic (diabetes, spinal cord injury, pelvic surgery), endocrine (hypogonadism, hyperprolactinemia), drug-induced, or psychogenic, and use preserved nocturnal erections to identify a psychogenic cause.
RE-13-D.usmle: Male and Transgender Reproductive System: Metabolic/regulatory and sexual dysfunction: erectile dysfunction; impotence

RE-13-D.t: Describe hematocele as blood within the tunica vaginalis after trauma, torsion, or tumor, and distinguish it from hydrocele by its failure to transilluminate.

Distinguish a communicating congenital hydrocele (patent processus vaginalis) from a noncommunicating hydrocele (infection, trauma, tumor), and identify a smooth scrotal fluid collection around the testis that transilluminates.
RE-13-D.usmle: Male and Transgender Reproductive System: Traumatic and mechanical: hydrocele (including neonatal)

RE-13-D.t: Describe spermatocele as a cystic dilation of the epididymis containing sperm, felt as a transilluminating mass separate from the testis, and compare it with a simple epididymal cyst.
RE-13-D.usmle: Male and Transgender Reproductive System: Traumatic and mechanical: spermatocele; epididymal cyst

RE-13-D.t: Explain varicocele as dilation of the pampiniform plexus, felt as a bag of worms that enlarges on standing and does not transilluminate, and relate it to infertility and, when new on the left, renal cell carcinoma.
RE-13-D.usmle: Male and Transgender Reproductive System: Traumatic and mechanical: varicocele

RE-13-D.t: Explain testicular torsion as twisting of the spermatic cord (bell-clapper deformity) causing venous then arterial occlusion, and identify sudden severe pain, a high-riding testis, and an absent cremasteric reflex.
RE-13-D.usmle: Male and Transgender Reproductive System: Traumatic and mechanical: torsion of testis

RE-13-D.t: Describe priapism as a painful erection lasting over 4 hours, with sickle cell disease and drugs as causes of the ischemic type, and predict cavernosal fibrosis and erectile dysfunction if it persists.
RE-13-D.usmle: Male and Transgender Reproductive System: Metabolic/regulatory and sexual dysfunction: priapism

RE-13-D.t: Describe Peyronie disease as a fibrous plaque of the tunica albuginea causing penile curvature and painful erection.
RE-13-D.usmle: Male and Transgender Reproductive System: Traumatic and mechanical: Peyronie disease

RE-13-D.t: Classify male infertility as pretesticular (hypogonadotropic hypogonadism), testicular (Klinefelter syndrome, cryptorchidism, varicocele, mumps orchitis), or post-testicular (obstruction, congenital bilateral absence of the vas deferens in cystic fibrosis).
RE-13-D.usmle: Male and Transgender Reproductive System: Metabolic/regulatory and sexual dysfunction: male factor infertility

RE-13-E.t: Distinguish nonproliferative fibrocystic change (cysts, apocrine metaplasia, fibrosis; no added cancer risk) from proliferative change without atypia (slightly raised risk) and atypical hyperplasia (moderately raised risk).
RE-13-E.usmle: Female and Transgender Reproductive System & Breast: Breast: Benign neoplasms: fibrocystic changes; breast cyst, solitary

RE-13-E.t: Describe galactocele as a milk-filled cystic dilation of a duct during lactation or weaning, and predict that it may rupture and cause local inflammation.

Describe mammary duct ectasia as dilated subareolar ducts with thick secretions and periductal chronic inflammation rich in plasma cells, in older multiparous women, and explain why nipple retraction can mimic carcinoma.
RE-13-E.usmle: Female and Transgender Reproductive System & Breast: Breast: Infectious, immunologic, and inflammatory: nipple discharge

RE-13-E.t: Explain acute mastitis as Staphylococcus aureus infection entering through nipple fissures during breastfeeding, with a red, painful, warm breast, fever, and possible abscess.
RE-13-E.usmle: Female and Transgender Reproductive System & Breast: Breast: Infectious, immunologic, and inflammatory: mastitis; breast abscess

RE-13-E.t: Describe periductal mastitis in smokers as squamous metaplasia of lactiferous ducts with keratin plugging, producing a painful subareolar mass or abscess.
RE-13-E.usmle: Female and Transgender Reproductive System & Breast: Breast: Infectious, immunologic, and inflammatory: inflammatory disease of breast

RE-13-E.t: Describe traumatic fat necrosis as nonenzymatic necrosis of breast fat after trauma or surgery, with foamy macrophages, giant cells, and calcification, forming a firm mass that can mimic carcinoma on exam and mammography.
RE-13-E.usmle: Female and Transgender Reproductive System & Breast: Breast: Infectious, immunologic, and inflammatory: fat necrosis

RE-13-E.t: Describe fibroadenoma as the most common benign breast tumor in young women, a small, firm, mobile mass of proliferating stroma and ducts that enlarges with estrogen in pregnancy.
RE-13-E.usmle: Female and Transgender Reproductive System & Breast: Breast: Benign neoplasms: fibroadenoma

RE-13-E.t: Distinguish phyllodes tumor (leaf-like projections of overgrown, hypercellular stroma, usually in older women, with potential to recur or metastasize) from fibroadenoma.
RE-13-E.usmle: Female and Transgender Reproductive System & Breast: Breast: Malignant neoplasms: phyllodes tumors

RE-13-E.t: Describe intraductal papilloma as a benign subareolar papillary growth in a large duct and identify it as a common cause of bloody nipple discharge.
RE-13-E.usmle: Female and Transgender Reproductive System & Breast: Breast: Benign neoplasms: intraductal papilloma

RE-13-E.t: Relate breast carcinoma risk to age, prolonged estrogen exposure (early menarche, late menopause, nulliparity, late first pregnancy, postmenopausal obesity), atypical hyperplasia, and family history, and identify the upper outer quadrant as the most common site.
RE-13-E.usmle: Female and Transgender Reproductive System & Breast: Breast: Malignant neoplasms: breast cancer

RE-13-E.t: Distinguish ductal carcinoma in situ (confined by basement membrane, mammographic microcalcifications, comedo necrosis) from invasive ductal carcinoma (most common type, firm stellate mass with desmoplastic stroma).
RE-13-E.usmle: Female and Transgender Reproductive System & Breast: Breast: Malignant neoplasms: intraductal carcinoma

RE-13-E.t: Explain lobular carcinoma as loss of E-cadherin (CDH1) causing discohesive cells that invade in single-file lines, and relate it to frequent bilateral and multifocal disease.
RE-13-E.usmle: Female and Transgender Reproductive System & Breast: Breast: Malignant neoplasms: breast cancer

RE-13-E.t: Describe Paget disease of the breast as eczematous nipple and areolar change from large Paget cells with clear cytoplasm in the epidermis, nearly always with underlying ductal carcinoma.
RE-13-E.usmle: Female and Transgender Reproductive System & Breast: Breast: Malignant neoplasms: Paget disease of breast

RE-13-E.t: Distinguish inflammatory breast carcinoma (tumor emboli in dermal lymphatics causing erythema, edema, and peau d'orange) from acute mastitis.
RE-13-E.usmle: Female and Transgender Reproductive System & Breast: Breast: Infectious, immunologic, and inflammatory: inflammatory disease of breast

RE-13-E.t: Distinguish gynecomastia (benign ductal and stromal proliferation from a raised estrogen to androgen ratio) from male breast carcinoma, and relate male breast carcinoma to BRCA2 mutation and Klinefelter syndrome.
RE-13-E.usmle: Male and Transgender Reproductive System: Neoplasms: breast cancer

RE-13-F.t: Explain benign prostatic hyperplasia as DHT-dependent nodular hyperplasia of glands and stroma in the transition (periurethral) zone of older men, and state that it is not a precursor of carcinoma.
RE-13-F.usmle: Male and Transgender Reproductive System: Traumatic and mechanical: benign prostatic hyperplasia

RE-13-F.t: Predict the urinary findings and complications of benign prostatic hyperplasia: hesitancy, weak stream, frequency, nocturia, urinary retention, bladder wall hypertrophy, infection, and hydronephrosis.
RE-13-F.usmle: Male and Transgender Reproductive System: Traumatic and mechanical: benign prostatic hyperplasia

RE-13-F.t: Identify E. coli and other gram-negative rods as the usual cause of acute bacterial prostatitis in older men (C. trachomatis and N. gonorrhoeae in younger men), with fever, chills, dysuria, and a tender, boggy prostate.
RE-13-F.usmle: Male and Transgender Reproductive System: Infectious, immunologic, and inflammatory: prostatitis

RE-13-F.t: Distinguish acute bacterial prostatitis from chronic bacterial prostatitis (recurrent urinary tract infection with the same organism) and chronic nonbacterial prostatitis (chronic pelvic pain without bacteria).
RE-13-F.usmle: Male and Transgender Reproductive System: Infectious, immunologic, and inflammatory: prostatitis

RE-13-G.t: Distinguish follicular cysts (unruptured follicle, may secrete estrogen), corpus luteum cysts (may hemorrhage into the peritoneum), and bilateral theca lutein cysts from high hCG in molar or multiple pregnancy.
RE-13-G.usmle: Female and Transgender Reproductive System & Breast: Neoplasms, benign and cystic: ovarian cyst

RE-13-G.t: Explain ovarian torsion as twisting of the ovary on its ligaments, usually when enlarged by a cyst or tumor, with venous then arterial occlusion causing sudden severe pelvic pain and possible infarction.
RE-13-G.usmle: Female and Transgender Reproductive System & Breast: Traumatic and mechanical: ovarian torsion

RE-13-G.t: Describe paraovarian cysts as thin-walled cysts in the broad ligament arising from Mullerian or Wolffian remnants, separate from the ovary, and predict torsion or rupture as complications.

Explain PCOS pathogenesis: raised LH to FSH ratio driving theca androgen, insulin resistance raising ovarian androgen and lowering SHBG, and arrested follicles forming multiple small peripheral ovarian cysts.
RE-13-G.usmle: Female and Transgender Reproductive System & Breast: Menstrual and endocrine: polycystic ovary syndrome

RE-13-G.t: Identify the findings and complications of PCOS: oligomenorrhea, hirsutism, acne, obesity, acanthosis nigricans, infertility, type 2 diabetes, dyslipidemia, and endometrial hyperplasia and carcinoma from unopposed estrogen.
RE-13-G.usmle: Female and Transgender Reproductive System & Breast: Menstrual and endocrine: polycystic ovary syndrome

RE-13-G.t: Describe tubo-ovarian cysts and abscesses as sequelae of PID in which an inflamed or fluid-filled tube adheres to the ovary, and predict rupture with peritonitis and later infertility.
RE-13-G.usmle: Female and Transgender Reproductive System & Breast: Infectious, immunologic, and inflammatory: salpingitis; oophoritis

RE-13-H.t: Compare complete mole (usually 46,XX, all paternal from an empty ovum, no fetal parts, diffuse villous swelling, p57 negative) with partial mole (triploid, fetal parts, focal swelling, p57 positive).
RE-13-H.usmle: Female and Transgender Reproductive System & Breast: Neoplasms, malignant and precancerous: gestational trophoblastic disease (hydatidiform mole)

RE-13-H.t: Predict the findings of complete hydatidiform mole: vaginal bleeding, uterus large for dates, very high hCG, hyperemesis, theca lutein cysts, hyperthyroidism, preeclampsia before 20 weeks, and higher choriocarcinoma risk.
RE-13-H.usmle: Female and Transgender Reproductive System & Breast: Neoplasms, malignant and precancerous: gestational trophoblastic disease (hydatidiform mole)

RE-13-H.t: Describe invasive mole as hydropic villi penetrating the myometrium, which can cause uterine perforation and hemorrhage and persistent hCG elevation after evacuation.
RE-13-H.usmle: Female and Transgender Reproductive System & Breast: Neoplasms, malignant and precancerous: gestational trophoblastic disease (hydatidiform mole)

RE-13-H.t: Describe gestational choriocarcinoma as malignant cytotrophoblast and syncytiotrophoblast without villi, arising after a mole, abortion, or normal pregnancy, with very high hCG and early hematogenous spread to lung, vagina, and brain.
RE-13-H.usmle: Female and Transgender Reproductive System & Breast: Neoplasms, malignant and precancerous: gestational trophoblastic disease (hydatidiform mole)

RE-13-H.t: Explain preeclampsia as abnormal placentation with failed spiral artery remodeling, placental ischemia, and release of antiangiogenic factors (sFlt-1, soluble endoglin) that cause maternal endothelial dysfunction.
RE-13-H.usmle: Pregnancy, Childbirth, & the Puerperium: Obstetric complications: preeclampsia, eclampsia, HELLP syndrome, gestational hypertension

RE-13-H.t: Identify preeclampsia as new hypertension (140/90 mm Hg or higher) after 20 weeks with proteinuria or end-organ damage, its risk factors (nulliparity, chronic hypertension, diabetes, multiple gestation), and its complications of eclampsia, HELLP syndrome, placental abruption, and fetal growth restriction.
RE-13-H.usmle: Pregnancy, Childbirth, & the Puerperium: Obstetric complications: preeclampsia, eclampsia, HELLP syndrome, gestational hypertension

RE-13-H.t: Distinguish placental abruption (premature separation with painful bleeding, linked to hypertension, cocaine, and trauma, risking DIC) from placenta previa (painless third-trimester bleeding).
RE-13-H.usmle: Pregnancy, Childbirth, & the Puerperium: Obstetric complications: placental abnormalities (abruptio placentae, placenta previa)

RE-13-H.t: Explain placenta accreta as villi attaching to or invading the myometrium through a deficient decidua basalis, with prior cesarean delivery and placenta previa as major risk factors.
RE-13-H.usmle: Pregnancy, Childbirth, & the Puerperium: Puerperium: retained placenta, products of conception (placenta accreta)

RE-13-H.t: Relate oligohydramnios to reduced fetal urine output (bilateral renal agenesis, urinary obstruction) with Potter sequence, and polyhydramnios to impaired fetal swallowing (esophageal atresia, anencephaly) or maternal diabetes.
RE-13-H.usmle: Pregnancy, Childbirth, & the Puerperium: Obstetric complications: polyhydramnios, oligohydramnios

RE-13-I.t: Describe a Bartholin cyst as obstruction of the Bartholin gland duct, forming a mass in the posterolateral vulvar vestibule that may become an abscess, and identify its occurrence in reproductive-age women.
RE-13-I.usmle: Female and Transgender Reproductive System & Breast: Infectious, immunologic, and inflammatory: Bartholin gland abscess

RE-13-I.t: Explain cystocele, urethrocele, and rectocele as herniation through weakened pelvic floor and endopelvic fascia, with risk factors of vaginal childbirth, aging, estrogen loss, obesity, and chronic straining or cough.
RE-13-I.usmle: Female and Transgender Reproductive System & Breast: Traumatic and mechanical: cystocele; rectocele; urethrocele

RE-13-I.t: Distinguish cystocele (bladder bulging into the anterior vaginal wall, incomplete emptying), urethrocele (urethra into the distal anterior wall, stress incontinence), and rectocele (rectum into the posterior wall, difficult defecation).
RE-13-I.usmle: Female and Transgender Reproductive System & Breast: Traumatic and mechanical: cystocele; rectocele; urethrocele

RE-13-J.t: Explain cervical intraepithelial neoplasia as high-risk HPV infection of the transformation zone with koilocytes, graded CIN 1 to 3 by the thickness of epithelium replaced by atypical immature cells (CIN 1 as LSIL, CIN 2 and 3 as HSIL).
RE-13-J.usmle: Female and Transgender Reproductive System & Breast: Neoplasms, malignant and precancerous: cervical dysplasia; abnormal cervical cytology

RE-13-J.t: Relate cervical dysplasia risk to persistent HPV 16 or 18 infection, many sexual partners, early sexual activity, smoking, and immunodeficiency such as HIV, and predict that most CIN 1 regresses.
RE-13-J.usmle: Female and Transgender Reproductive System & Breast: Neoplasms, malignant and precancerous: HPV-caused dysplasia

RE-13-J.t: Describe invasive cervical carcinoma (mostly squamous cell, some adenocarcinoma) with postcoital bleeding, and explain how lateral spread can obstruct the ureters, causing hydronephrosis and renal failure.
RE-13-J.usmle: Female and Transgender Reproductive System & Breast: Neoplasms, malignant and precancerous: cervical cancer

RE-13-J.t: Relate endometrial hyperplasia to unopposed estrogen (obesity, anovulation, PCOS, estrogen-only therapy, granulosa cell tumor) and PTEN loss, and identify atypical hyperplasia as the precursor of endometrioid carcinoma.
RE-13-J.usmle: Female and Transgender Reproductive System & Breast: Neoplasms, malignant and precancerous: endometrial hyperplasia

RE-13-J.t: Compare endometrioid endometrial carcinoma (estrogen-related, arising from hyperplasia, PTEN and Lynch syndrome mutations) with serous carcinoma (older women, atrophic endometrium, TP53 mutation, aggressive), both presenting with postmenopausal bleeding.
RE-13-J.usmle: Female and Transgender Reproductive System & Breast: Neoplasms, malignant and precancerous: endometrial/uterine cancer

RE-13-J.t: Describe endometrial and endocervical polyps as benign localized overgrowths of glands and stroma that cause abnormal or intermenstrual bleeding.
RE-13-J.usmle: Female and Transgender Reproductive System & Breast: Neoplasms, benign and cystic: endometrial polyps; endocervical polyps

RE-13-J.t: Describe leiomyoma as a benign, estrogen-sensitive, well-circumscribed smooth muscle tumor with a whorled pattern, more common in Black women, causing heavy bleeding, pelvic pressure, anemia, and infertility.
RE-13-J.usmle: Female and Transgender Reproductive System & Breast: Neoplasms, benign and cystic: leiomyomata uteri

RE-13-J.t: Distinguish leiomyosarcoma (arising de novo in older women, a single large soft mass with necrosis, nuclear atypia, and high mitotic rate) from leiomyoma, which does not transform into it.
RE-13-J.usmle: Musculoskeletal System: Neoplasms, malignant: leiomyosarcoma

RE-13-J.t: Relate prostate adenocarcinoma to age, Black race, family history, and BRCA2, and explain its origin in the peripheral zone, Gleason grading by gland pattern, and raised PSA.
RE-13-J.usmle: Male and Transgender Reproductive System: Neoplasms: prostate cancer

RE-13-J.t: Predict osteoblastic bone metastases of prostate carcinoma to the lumbar spine and pelvis through the vertebral venous plexus, with bone pain and raised alkaline phosphatase.
RE-13-J.usmle: Male and Transgender Reproductive System: Neoplasms: prostate cancer

RE-13-J.t: Classify ovarian tumors by origin as surface epithelial (serous, mucinous, endometrioid, clear cell, Brenner), germ cell (teratoma, dysgerminoma, yolk sac tumor, choriocarcinoma), or sex cord-stromal (granulosa cell, Sertoli-Leydig cell, fibroma, thecoma).
RE-13-J.usmle: Female and Transgender Reproductive System & Breast: Neoplasms, benign and cystic: benign neoplasm of ovary

RE-13-J.t: Relate high-grade serous ovarian carcinoma to BRCA1, BRCA2, and TP53 mutations and the fallopian tube fimbria, and identify psammoma bodies, raised CA-125, ascites, and peritoneal and omental spread.
RE-13-J.usmle: Female and Transgender Reproductive System & Breast: Neoplasms, malignant and precancerous: ovarian cancer

RE-13-J.t: Identify mature cystic teratoma (most common ovarian germ cell tumor), struma ovarii (a monodermal teratoma of thyroid tissue that can cause hyperthyroidism), dysgerminoma (sheets of clear cells, raised LDH), and yolk sac tumor (Schiller-Duval bodies, raised AFP).
RE-13-J.usmle: Female and Transgender Reproductive System & Breast: Neoplasms, malignant and precancerous: ovarian cancer

RE-13-J.t: Predict the effects of hormonally active ovarian stromal tumors: granulosa cell tumor (estrogen, Call-Exner bodies, precocious puberty or endometrial hyperplasia), Sertoli-Leydig cell tumor (virilization), and fibroma with ascites and hydrothorax (Meigs syndrome).
RE-13-J.usmle: Female and Transgender Reproductive System & Breast: Neoplasms, benign and cystic: benign neoplasm of ovary

RE-13-J.t: Identify Krukenberg tumor as bilateral ovarian metastasis of signet ring cell adenocarcinoma, most often from the stomach.
Relate squamous cell carcinoma of the penis to HPV 16, lack of circumcision, phimosis, and smoking, and identify Bowen disease, erythroplasia of Queyrat, and bowenoid papulosis as carcinoma in situ.
RE-13-J.usmle: Male and Transgender Reproductive System: Neoplasms: penile cancer

RE-13-J.t: Classify testicular tumors as germ cell (most, with isochromosome 12p and germ cell neoplasia in situ) or sex cord-stromal, and identify a painless firm mass that does not transilluminate, with cryptorchidism and Klinefelter syndrome as risks.
RE-13-J.usmle: Male and Transgender Reproductive System: Neoplasms: testicular cancer

RE-13-J.t: Distinguish seminoma (most common, uniform clear cells with lymphocytes, placental alkaline phosphatase, radiosensitive, good prognosis) from embryonal carcinoma, yolk sac tumor (AFP), choriocarcinoma (hCG), and teratoma.
RE-13-J.usmle: Male and Transgender Reproductive System: Neoplasms: testicular cancer

RE-13-J.t: Describe Leydig cell tumor (Reinke crystals, androgen or estrogen excess causing precocious puberty or gynecomastia) and testicular lymphoma as the most common testicular tumor in men over 60.
RE-13-J.usmle: Male and Transgender Reproductive System: Neoplasms: testicular cancer

RE-13-J.t: Distinguish vaginal squamous cell carcinoma (older women, HPV, vaginal intraepithelial neoplasia), clear cell adenocarcinoma (in utero DES exposure), and embryonal rhabdomyosarcoma (sarcoma botryoides, grape-like mass in young girls, desmin positive).
RE-13-J.usmle: Female and Transgender Reproductive System & Breast: Neoplasms, malignant and precancerous: neoplasms of the vulva, vagina, cervix, uterus, or ovaries

RE-13-J.t: Compare HPV-related vulvar squamous cell carcinoma (younger women, from HPV-related intraepithelial neoplasia) with HPV-independent vulvar carcinoma (older women, lichen sclerosus, differentiated VIN with TP53 mutation).
RE-13-J.usmle: Female and Transgender Reproductive System & Breast: Neoplasms, malignant and precancerous: vulvar dysplasia and cancer

RE-13-J.t: Distinguish usual (HPV-related) vulvar intraepithelial neoplasia from differentiated VIN, and distinguish extramammary Paget disease of the vulva (intraepithelial adenocarcinoma, usually without underlying carcinoma) from Paget disease of the breast.
RE-13-J.usmle: Female and Transgender Reproductive System & Breast: Neoplasms, malignant and precancerous: vulvar dysplasia and cancer

RE-13-K.t: Distinguish chancroid (Haemophilus ducreyi; painful ulcer with ragged edges and gray exudate, painful suppurative inguinal nodes) from the painless indurated chancre of primary syphilis.
RE-13-K.usmle: Female and Transgender Reproductive System & Breast: Infectious, immunologic, and inflammatory: chancroid (Haemophilus ducreyi)

RE-13-K.t: Explain bacterial vaginosis as replacement of lactobacilli by Gardnerella vaginalis and anaerobes, causing thin gray discharge with fishy odor, pH above 4.5, positive amine (whiff) test, clue cells, and few neutrophils.
RE-13-K.usmle: Female and Transgender Reproductive System & Breast: Infectious, immunologic, and inflammatory: bacterial vaginosis

RE-13-K.t: Use vaginal pH, the KOH whiff test, and wet mount findings to distinguish bacterial vaginosis, trichomoniasis, and candidal vaginitis.
RE-13-K.usmle: Female and Transgender Reproductive System & Breast: Infectious, immunologic, and inflammatory: vaginitis; vulvovaginitis

RE-13-K.t: Identify genital chlamydial infection as often asymptomatic and the cause of urethritis, cervicitis, epididymitis, PID, reactive arthritis, and neonatal conjunctivitis and pneumonia.
RE-13-K.usmle: Female and Transgender Reproductive System & Breast: Infectious, immunologic, and inflammatory: sexually transmitted infections and exposure

RE-13-K.t: Describe lymphogranuloma venereum (C. trachomatis L1 to L3) as a small painless genital ulcer followed by painful inguinal lymphadenopathy (buboes) and possible proctocolitis.
RE-13-K.usmle: Female and Transgender Reproductive System & Breast: Infectious, immunologic, and inflammatory: lymphogranuloma venereum (Chlamydia trachomatis)

RE-13-K.t: Identify gonococcal urethritis with purulent discharge and intracellular gram-negative diplococci, cervicitis, PID, neonatal conjunctivitis, and disseminated infection (septic arthritis, tenosynovitis, pustules), and relate recurrent infection to C5 to C9 deficiency.
RE-13-K.usmle: Female and Transgender Reproductive System & Breast: Infectious, immunologic, and inflammatory: gonorrhea (Neisseria gonorrhoeae)

RE-13-K.t: Describe genital herpes as painful grouped vesicles that ulcerate, with systemic symptoms in primary infection, recurrence from sacral ganglia, multinucleated giant cells, and neonatal infection acquired during delivery.
RE-13-K.usmle: Female and Transgender Reproductive System & Breast: Infectious, immunologic, and inflammatory: genital herpes

RE-13-K.t: Distinguish condylomata acuminata (HPV 6 and 11, koilocytes) from condylomata lata of secondary syphilis, and relate high-risk HPV to cervical, vulvar, vaginal, penile, anal, and oropharyngeal carcinoma.
RE-13-K.usmle: Female and Transgender Reproductive System & Breast: Infectious, immunologic, and inflammatory: condylomata acuminata; genital/venereal/anal warts

RE-13-K.t: Identify the causes of nongonococcal urethritis (C. trachomatis most often, also Mycoplasma genitalium, Ureaplasma urealyticum, Trichomonas vaginalis), and relate it to reactive arthritis with conjunctivitis in HLA-B27-positive men.
RE-13-K.usmle: Male and Transgender Reproductive System: Infectious, immunologic, and inflammatory: chlamydial and nonchlamydial nongonococcal urethritis

RE-13-K.t: Describe the stages of syphilis: primary painless chancre, secondary rash on palms and soles with condylomata lata and lymphadenopathy, latency, and tertiary gummas, aortitis of the ascending aorta, and tabes dorsalis.
RE-13-K.usmle: Female and Transgender Reproductive System & Breast: Infectious, immunologic, and inflammatory: syphilis (Treponema pallidum)

RE-13-K.t: Interpret nontreponemal tests (VDRL, RPR; anticardiolipin antibodies, false positives in pregnancy, SLE, and viral infection) and treponemal tests (FTA-ABS, which stays positive for life) in syphilis.
RE-13-K.usmle: Female and Transgender Reproductive System & Breast: Infectious, immunologic, and inflammatory: syphilis (Treponema pallidum)

RE-13-K.t: Identify the findings of congenital syphilis: rhinitis (snuffles), rash, saddle nose, Hutchinson teeth, mulberry molars, saber shins, and sensorineural deafness.
RE-13-K.usmle: Pregnancy, Childbirth, & the Puerperium: Prenatal care: infections, maternal, fetal, newborn

RE-13-K.t: Explain toxic shock syndrome as TSST-1 superantigen release by S. aureus (retained tampons, nasal packing, wounds) causing polyclonal T cell cytokine release, fever, hypotension, diffuse rash with later palm and sole desquamation, and multiorgan injury.
RE-13-K.usmle: Multisystem Processes & Disorders: Infectious disorders: bacterial: toxic shock syndrome

RE-13-K.t: Describe trichomoniasis as a sexually transmitted flagellated protozoan infection causing frothy yellow-green malodorous discharge, strawberry cervix, pH above 4.5, and motile trophozoites on wet mount.
RE-13-K.usmle: Female and Transgender Reproductive System & Breast: Infectious, immunologic, and inflammatory: trichomoniasis (Trichomonas vaginalis)
